executive_summary.problem_statement: Flask + SQLAlchemy + Redis system experiences UI/UX desynchronization where follow button state becomes inconsistent between frontend, cache, and database. Users see 'Follow' despite existing database records, or vice versa.
root_causes: Frontend performs optimistic UI updates before backend HTTP 200 confirmation
API follows Redis cache blindly without DB verification on mismatch
Redis cache keys lack tenant_id prefix, causing cross-tenant data leakage
No soft-delete support; deleted rows still cached and returned as active
Concurrent follow/unfollow operations lack atomic guarantees
Missing composite unique constraint allows duplicate relationship entries
executive_summary.solution_summary: Added tenant_id to schema, implemented cache reconciliation in API, modified frontend to wait for confirmation, added soft-delete support with proper filtering, and introduced atomic transactions with idempotent error handling.

tests.name: UI stays correct despite Redis cache delay
tests.scenario: User follows, backend inserts to DB, Redis has 2-second write delay, user refreshes during delay
tests.expected_behavior: API detects cache miss and queries DB, returns true despite stale cache, UI shows 'Following'
tests.observed_behavior: ✓ Cache reconciliation successful - DB is source of truth
tests.fix_applied: follow_status() now compares cache with DB and reconciles drift

tests.name: Concurrent rapid toggles result in consistent final state
tests.scenario: Rapid follow/unfollow/follow (3 actions in 150ms), DB and Redis diverge
tests.expected_behavior: Final state should be following=true, cache and DB consistent after reconciliation
tests.observed_behavior: ✓ Final state correct - DB and cache both show following=true
tests.fix_applied: Atomic DB operations, proper cache invalidation on each change

tests.name: Redis keys properly scoped by tenant
tests.scenario: Tenant 1 and Tenant 2 with same numeric user IDs, old keys have no tenant prefix
tests.expected_behavior: Tenant isolation maintained, each tenant sees only their own follow relationships
tests.observed_behavior: ✓ Tenant 1 and Tenant 2 properly isolated - no cross-tenant data leakage

tests.name: Soft-deleted relationships not returned as active
tests.scenario: Admin soft-deletes follow relationship, cache still has stale value=1
tests.expected_behavior: API queries DB and filters deleted rows, returns false even if cache says 1
tests.observed_behavior: ✓ Soft-delete properly handled - DB filters deleted rows, cache drift reconciled
tests.root_cause_addressed: No soft-delete support, cache staleness after delete
tests.fix_applied: Added deleted column, get_follower() filters WHERE deleted=FALSE

tests.name: Frontend waits for backend confirmation before updating UI
tests.scenario: Frontend optimistic update without waiting for HTTP 200, backend returns 500 on duplicate
tests.expected_behavior: Frontend shows loading spinner, waits for 200, rolls back on error
tests.observed_behavior: ✓ Frontend properly handles async confirmation, backend returns idempotent 200
tests.root_cause_addressed: Premature optimistic UI update without confirmation
tests.fix_applied: Frontend waits for HTTP 200, backend returns idempotent 200 on duplicate

schema_changes.migration_name: Add tenant isolation and soft-delete support to followers table
schema_changes.previous_ddl: CREATE TABLE followers (follower_id INTEGER NOT NULL, followed_id INTEGER NOT NULL);
schema_changes.new_ddl:
CREATE TABLE followers (
    id SERIAL PRIMARY KEY,
    tenant_id INTEGER NOT NULL,
    follower_id INTEGER NOT NULL,
    followed_id INTEGER NOT NULL,
    deleted BOOLEAN DEFAULT FALSE,
    created_at TIMESTAMP DEFAULT CURRENT_TIMESTAMP,
    updated_at TIMESTAMP DEFAULT CURRENT_TIMESTAMP,
    CONSTRAINT uq_followers_tenant_user UNIQUE(tenant_id, follower_id, followed_id),
    CONSTRAINT fk_followers_tenant FOREIGN KEY(tenant_id) REFERENCES tenants(id) ON DELETE CASCADE
);

improvements.previous_behavior: Returns Redis value blindly, ignores DB state, no tenant isolation
improvements.new_behavior: Cache reconciliation logic: check DB on miss/mismatch, DB is source of truth
changes: Cache key now includes tenant_id for isolation
On cache hit: compares with DB to detect drift
On cache miss: queries DB and populates cache
Fallback: on Redis error, uses DB only
Logging at every step for debugging

improvements.previous_behavior: Inserts without checks, returns immediately without confirmation
improvements.new_behavior: Atomic with error handling, idempotent on duplicate
changes: Attempts DB insert with composite unique constraint
On success: updates cache and returns HTTP 200
On IntegrityError: checks current state and returns idempotent 200
Proper error responses for client handling
All operations logged for audit trail

improvements.new_behavior: Soft-delete with proper invalidation and audit trail
changes: Idempotent: returns 200 even if already deleted

improvements.impact: Prevents cross-tenant data leakage in Redis

improvements.previous: Optimistic state change before API confirmation
improvements.new: Three separate states: isFollowing (from server), isLoading (request in flight), error (for feedback)
Calls fetchFollowStatus() on mount, fetches actual state from server

improvements.previous: Updates UI immediately, no confirmation wait
improvements.new: Shows loading spinner, waits for HTTP 200, only then updates UI
Rolls back UI on error, displays error message (with type-specific text)

improvements.previous: No tenant context in API calls
improvements.new: Passes tenantId to all API endpoints
